title: “Venerable sirs, what is the effort of abandoning? Here, a monk does not consent to arisen sensual thought; he abandons, dispels, destroys, makes it non-existent.…
content: “Venerable sirs, what is the effort of abandoning? Here, a monk does not consent to arisen sensual thought; he abandons, dispels, destroys, makes it non-existent. He does not consent to arisen ill-will thought … he does not consent to arisen harmful thought; he abandons, dispels, destroys, makes it non-existent. This, venerable sirs, is called the effort of abandoning.”

title: Then the Venerable Ānanda went to that nun, sat down on the prepared seat, and said to her: “Sister, this body is produced by food,…
content: Then the Venerable Ānanda went to that nun, sat down on the prepared seat, and said to her: “Sister, this body is produced by food, depends on food. Food should be abandoned. Sister, this body is produced by craving, depends on craving. Craving should be abandoned. Sister, this body is produced by conceit, depends on conceit. Conceit should be abandoned. Sister, this body is produced by sexual intercourse, depends on sexual intercourse. Sexual intercourse — the breaking of the bridge — has been spoken of by the Blessed One. ‘Sister, this body is produced by food, depends on food. Food should be abandoned.’ Thus it has been said. For what reason was this said?”

title: “‘My mind will be internally established, well fixed. Evil, unwholesome states that arise will not invade my mind and will not stand.’ Thus, monk, you…
content: “‘My mind will be internally established, well fixed. Evil, unwholesome states that arise will not invade my mind and will not stand.’ Thus, monk, you should train.”

title: “Monks, these five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless. What five? The…
content: “Monks, these five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless. What five? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of peril, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world. These five perceptions, monks, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless.”

title: The foolish, ignorant person delights in heedlessness, But the wise one guards heedlessness as his greatest treasure. Do not yield to heedlessness, do not yield…
content:
The foolish, ignorant person delights in heedlessness,
But the wise one guards heedlessness as his greatest treasure.
Do not yield to heedlessness, do not yield to sensual pleasures.

title: All conditioned things are truly impermanent, They arise and then pass away — Their nature is always thus. They come into being, Then they again…
content:
All conditioned things are truly impermanent,
They arise and then pass away —
Their nature is always thus.
They come into being,
Then they again are destroyed.
Blissful indeed when they
Are calmed and at peace.

title: - “Lust, Venerable Bharadvāja, is the mind. Sometimes, even toward those who are like mothers, lust arises. Toward those like sisters, lust arises. Toward those…
content: - “Lust, Venerable Bharadvāja, is the mind. Sometimes, even toward those who are like mothers, lust arises. Toward those like sisters, lust arises. Toward those like daughters, lust arises. Bharadvāja, is there another cause, another reason why these young monks … live the holy life completely?” - “Great king, the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has said: ‘Come, monks, contemplate this body from the soles of the feet upward, from the top of the head downward, enclosed by skin and full of various impurities. In this body there are: head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, diaphragm, spleen, lungs, intestines, intestinal mesentery, stomach, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, skin oil, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, urine.’ This, great king, is the cause, this is the reason why these young monks live the perfectly pure holy life for their whole life, completing it fully.”

title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline, as lack of clear comprehension. For…
content: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline, as lack of clear comprehension. For one lacking clear comprehension, monks, unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline.”

title: Four wheels, nine doors, Full of defilement, tied by greed — Mired in mud, O great hero, What will be the future state Of such…
content:
Four wheels, nine doors,
Full of defilement, tied by greed —
Mired in mud,
O great hero,
What will be the future state
Of such a human birth?

(The Blessed One):
Having cut off delight and bondage,
Sensual desire and evil,
Having destroyed the root of craving —
Such will be his future state.

title: “Monks, through lust, one is not freed. Through lust for form, monks, consciousness becomes established with a foothold. With form as its object, with form…
content: “Monks, through lust, one is not freed. Through lust for form, monks, consciousness becomes established with a foothold. With form as its object, with form as its support, seeking delight, it grows, increases, and expands. Through lust for feeling … for perception … for formations, monks, consciousness becomes established with a foothold. With formations as its object, with formations as its support, seeking delight, it grows, increases, and expands. Monks, if anyone says: ‘Apart from form, apart from feeling, apart from perception, apart from formations, I will show the coming and going, the passing away and arising, the growth, increase, and expansion of consciousness’ — such a thing is not possible. Monks, if a monk has abandoned lust for the form element — with the abandonment of lust, the basis is cut off, the support of consciousness does not exist. If a monk has abandoned lust for the feeling element … for the perception element … for the formation element … Monks, if a monk has abandoned lust for the consciousness element — with the abandonment of lust, the basis is cut off, the support of consciousness does not exist. Without that support, consciousness does not expand, does not generate activity, and is liberated. Being liberated, it is steady; being steady, it is content; being content, it is not agitated; being not agitated, he personally attains Nibbāna. He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”
